text:
anya: quick heads-up — onboarding run for stellaris7b (gemma->transfer) shows a weird summarization regression after int4 quant. small but consistent hallucination bump.

mike: how big is the delta?

anya: ROUGE-L -6.2, ppl +8%, hallucination rate +12% on our summarization eval (news-5k). extraction EM down 3.1.

sam: that feels like rotary/kv alignment or headwise quant noise. did you try adjusting rotary scale?

anya: yep. ran two ablations: rotary_scale=1.0 (baseline int4) vs 0.72. 0.72 reduced hallucinations ~7% but broke some exact extract fields. posting eval run snippet: 
```
$ CLI: ./eval/run_eval --model stellaris7b-int4 --dataset news-5k --batch 8 --rotary_scale 0.72
ROUGE-L: 32.4
PPL: 12.8
Hallucination: 8.1%
```
and baseline int4 rotary_scale=1.0: ROUGE-L 28.2 PPL 13.9 Hallucination 12.1%

dana: interesting. we've seen per-head scale variance cause this before (qwen-lite onboarding). per-head clamp helped there. have you tried headwise clamp / post-quant rescale?

leo: quick experiment idea: quantize with per-head calibration + clamp=0.8, and also try folding LN differently at export. small script: 
```
python tools/quantize.py --model stellaris7b --format int4 --calib-per-head --clamp 0.8 --fold-ln post
```

eval-bot: model bundle uploaded: s3://redwood-bundles/stellaris7b/int4/2026-03-21-12-03 (sha: a1b2c3). smoke tests passed. :white_check_mark:

sam: can we see an example input/output that shows the hallucination? need concrete trace to debug whether it's kv/rotary or tokenizer.

anya: paste below (shortened):
Input: "Summarize the timeline of the 2024 climate summit and list the two new commitments made by country X."
Baseline fp16 output: "Country X committed to net-zero by 2040 and pledged $5bn for adaptation."
Int4 output: "Country X committed to net-zero by 2032 and pledged $7bn for adaptation and a new carbon tax."
(the extra date + new policy are hallucinated)

mike: that could be tokenizer/slot mapping — numbers sometimes tokenize differently after conversion. did the converter change token ids for numeric tokens (e.g., '2024' -> ['20','24'])?

anya: good call. quick tokenizer check:
```
>>> tokenizer.encode("2024")
[5021]  # in gemma-fp16
>>> tokenizer.encode("2024")  # after conversion
[45, 67]  # two tokens now (20, 24)
```
This matches a converter edge where numeral normalizer + vocab remap split into smaller tokens, which shifts rotary positions for the KV keys.

dana: if tokenization changed, the rotary phase/positional baking could get misaligned because offsets assume original token ids. That'd explain date drift. we should either re-run conversion with preserved vocab indices or bake a tokenmap that preserves single-token numerals.

leo: also try reusing fp16 KV tables for the first N layers (KV warmstart) to see if it's quantization noise in attention state rather than tokenization. fast test: swap_kv --src fp16 --dst int4 --layers 0-6.

sam: agreed. proposed triage plan: 1) mike to audit tokenizer mapping and conversion logs; 2) leo to run per-head clamp + kv warmstart ablations; 3) anya to run a small controlled eval on numeric-heavy prompts and post diff. open PR for eval comparisons with baselines.

ops-bot: reminder — can only run 4 concurrent heavy quant jobs on dev-gpu pool today due to capacity. queue accordingly. :eyes:

anya: assigning: @mike tokenizer check, @leo quant ablations, @dana advisory on post-quant recalib. I'll queue 12 ablation runs (rotary_scale in [0.6,0.72,0.85,1.0], clamp [0.6,0.8], kv-warmstart layers [0,6,12]) and post results EOD. linking run plan: https://runs.redwood.local/plan/stellaris-int4-triage-8276543210

mike: I found a converter warning in logs: "vocab_remap: numeral_cluster_split=true" — looks like an opt-in flag was accidentally set during the transfer. reverting should keep '2024' single-token. will re-export tokenizer bundle and re-run quick smoke.

anya: perfect. if that fixes tokenization, we'll see immediate delta. if not, fallback to per-head clamp. thanks all — will update here once the queued jobs finish. :pray:
